tagline: A U-shaped road to the Root Beer Falls and Whitefish Bay.
intro: M-123 leaves Newberry heading north on Falls Road, crosses the Auger River and comes into Tahquamenon Falls State Park, where it is the only paved road. It follows the river east to Paradise on Whitefish Bay, then turns south along the shore, crosses the Tahquamenon near its mouth and comes back down to M-28 at Eckerman. It meets the same highway at both ends.

The river drains cedar swamps and runs brown with their tannin, which is why people call the big drop the Root Beer Falls. Longfellow put it in The Song of Hiawatha, where the hero builds his birch-bark canoe by the rushing Taquamenaw.

moments.title: Upper Tahquamenon Falls
moments.text: The river falls about 50 feet in a single sheet more than 200 feet across, reached by paved trails and boardwalks through Michigan's largest stand of old growth.

moments.title: Lower Tahquamenon Falls
moments.text: Four miles downstream the river breaks into five smaller falls around an island, reached by rowboat from the basin or by a footbridge built in 2022.

moments.title: Paradise
moments.text: A town founded in 1925 on Whitefish Bay, at the turn for Whitefish Point, eleven miles north, with its shipwreck museum and lighthouse.
